rationale: PINS class-EXPRESSION members and the single owner rule (R1). Pre-fix `const A = class Inner { m() {} }` produced NO member at all — the variable path's only descent trigger tested for `object`, so a class value never descended and the whole body was lost: no member symbol, no `contains` edge, and the calls inside `m` attributed to the enclosing function. The javascript twin emitted `method:m` all along and the oracle derives nothing for the shape, so no differential could ever have flagged it: the twin was the only available reference. The owner rule is the twin's, ported: a class expression's own declared name wins, else the binding it initialises or assigns to; an object literal is owned by its binding; a function boundary ends the search; a value with no binding to name stays OWNERLESS, which is correct silence rather than a gap — so the call-argument and returned forms are pinned as ownerless precisely so a future 'fix' cannot attach them to whatever encloses them. THE SECOND HALF: the same rule now names the relationship SOURCE as well as the symbol. The resolver used to walk up to the nearest variable_declarator with no function-boundary check, so a method inside a RETURNED object literal matched nothing and every call in it was charged to the enclosing method too — the same call sitting in two payloads and the edge naming the wrong source (`prepare->get`). The `inner` notIncludes pin is the only shape that can tell 'omitted' from 'double-counted'. KNOWN DIVERGENCE, recorded not adopted: for the NAMED class expression the twin emits a `contains` edge `Inner->usesHelper` whose SOURCE has no symbol in either analyzer, because a class expression creates no symbol. This analyzer requires the owner to exist, so it emits no such edge. Making the twins agree needs a ruling on whether a class expression should be a symbol; until then the payload and the calls edge are pinned and the dangling edge is deliberately absent. R9 UPDATE: the named-class-expression divergence recorded below is now RESOLVED. The ruling is that `class Inner {...}` is a class declaration wherever it appears, so the class becomes a symbol and its members' containment edge becomes joinable in both twins. The anonymous form is unchanged by design: with no name of its own, its members belong to the binding that holds the value.

expectSymbols.name: Inner
expectSymbols.note: R9: a NAMED class expression is a class declaration, so it is a Class symbol. Its absence was the root cause of the forbidden edge above: the member's owner (`Inner`) resolved to nothing, so addContainmentRelationships dropped the edge and the class was invisible as a type. The ANONYMOUS class expression below deliberately stays a bag of members owned by the binding \u2014 it has no name of its own.

anonymous class expression: owned by the binding
the assignment form (how a svelte custom-element base is written) — ownerless pre-fix

object-literal assignment, newly owned via the same rule

expectRelationships.note: RESOLVED DIVERGENCE, and this pin used to be a FORBID. When R1 landed it recorded the javascript twin's `contains Inner->usesHelper` as a KNOWN DIVERGENCE and deliberately did not adopt it, because adopting it required a ruling this fixture did not have: whether a named class expression should be a SYMBOL at all. Without one, `Inner` named no symbol, so the edge had a target no index could join and typescript dropped it. R9 is that ruling \u2014 a class expression carrying a name is a class DECLARATION (the name is written in the file and is in scope inside its own body, where `new Inner()` already resolved to it). So `Inner` is now a Class symbol, the owner resolves, and the edge is real in both twins. Pinned as a positive now, and `Inner` is asserted as a class symbol below.
